task: The selected compatible, shut member interfaces must join local group 1 and initiate LACP negotiation. Configure their channel membership.

teaching.hint: Choose LACP’s initiating mode, not static aggregation.
teaching.takeaway: Active sends LACP negotiation. It can pair with active or passive, but the members and peer must still be compatible.

task: The selected compatible member interfaces must join group 1 and respond to LACP without initiating it. The peer is already configured active.

teaching.hint: A responding LACP mode works when the peer initiates.
teaching.takeaway: Passive is a negotiation role, not a standby-only traffic link. Two passive peers cannot initiate formation.

task: A ping crosses the link, but you must check whether both intended members actually joined LACP. Display bundle state and member flags.

teaching.hint: Inspect the aggregate and each member, not just connectivity.
teaching.takeaway: A port channel marked in use can have fewer active members than intended. Read the legend and count bundled members rather than stopping at the logical up state.

task: Two intended member links may reach different devices. Display their learned LACP partner system and port information.

teaching.hint: Use protocol-partner evidence, not only local group numbers.
teaching.takeaway: Both members should identify the intended common partner system, with the appropriate remote ports. Matching local channel-group numbers alone does not establish that relationship.

task: Po1 is an existing Layer 2 bundle. Enter its logical interface configuration to apply a common trunk change.

teaching.hint: Select the aggregate, rather than editing only one physical member.
teaching.takeaway: Apply common VLAN changes through the logical port channel and verify the resulting member settings. A one-member change can create inconsistency.

task: On a multilayer switch supporting routed EtherChannel, Port-channel1 is selected. Convert that logical interface to Layer 3 before assigning its transit address.

teaching.hint: The bundle’s logical interface must have the same routed role as its members.
teaching.takeaway: Put the transit IP address on the logical port channel. Physical members must be routed and should not each receive another address from that transit subnet.

task: In the isolated lab, this shut physical interface belongs to group 1. Remove its channel membership before changing the aggregation method.

teaching.hint: Remove the membership on the physical interface, not the entire logical interface.
teaching.takeaway: This detaches the selected member. Reapply the intended method with compatible settings and verify both ends before restoring traffic.
